newsitem.title: GERMANY: Schering seeking to raise dividend payout.
newsitem.headline: Schering seeking to raise dividend payout.

text.p: Schering AG chief financial officer Klaus Pohle said on Thursday that the German pharmaceuticals group was seeking to keep its dividend increases in line with rising profits.

In an interview with Reuters Financial Television, Pohle also said that Schering hoped sales of its multiple sclerosis drug Betaferon would double for the full-year from the 1997 first half level of 327 million marks ($173 million).
"We do think that the increase in the dividend will be in line with the increase in profit," Pohle said when asked to make a prediction about the group's dividend payout.
Pohle said Schering had been successful in the first half with Betaferon, which was one of the engines behind the group's 21 percent jump in first half sales to 3.1 billion marks.
"Naturally we would like to repeat this success in the second half," he said.
He said Schering was seeking to broaden its product range and noted increased research spending in the second half.

"We would like to broaden it and we will do everything we can in our research efforts," he said. "Our cost of research in second quarter has gone up," Pohle said, explaining however that new product launches were some time away. " Most of the products will come in 1999 and 2000."
